# Pack field reference

Every field a pack `.json` file can declare. If you're building a pack in the
in-app editor you mostly won't need this page -- the editor's pickers already
constrain you to valid values. This is for editing pack JSON directly, or
understanding what the editor's fields actually write.

Current pack schema version: **1**.

## Manifest

`manifest` identifies the pack. The engine only reads `id` (must match
`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`) and `version`; everything else is for humans and the
pack-picker UI.

| field | required | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | lowercase-hyphen slug, must be unique among installed packs |
| `name` | yes | shown in the pack picker |
| `version` | yes | free-form, e.g. `"1.0.0"` |
| `authors` | no | array of strings |
| `license` | no | e.g. `"CC-BY-4.0"` |
| `attribution` | no | required by the validator (as a warning) if `license` starts with `CC-BY` |
| `description` | no | shown under the pack in the picker |
| `systemTag` | no | free text, e.g. `"5e"` -- the engine never reads this |
| `minEngineSchema` | no | defaults to the current schema version |

## Cells

`cells.colors` must hold **exactly 10** entries (one per tesseract), each
`{ hex, name }`. Color is normally the only in-fiction tell for which tesseract
the party currently stands in, so the validator warns (not errors) on
duplicate hex values.

## Rooms

Two top-level maps, keyed by slug: `rooms` (authored, singleton by default)
and `fillerRooms` (repeatable, used to fill out the dungeon to 40). A pack
needs a **minimum of three rooms**: one `start`, one `exit`, and one filler
template.

An id may not appear in both maps.

### Reading order

| field | read by | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | GM UI / log | warned if empty |
| `read` | players, verbatim | warned if empty |
| `detail` | players, on request | what a closer look reveals |
| `gm` | GM only | never shown to players |
| `orientation` | GM only | the room's spatial gimmick -- this app's whole subject |

`read`, `detail`, `gm`, `orientation`, and `onKey.*` all support
`{{key}}` template substitution -- see **Template vars** below.

### Creatures and features

`creatures: []` and `features: []` are lists of `{ id, name, ..., resetsOn }`.
Every entry automatically becomes a trackable GM-facing action -- you do not
author actions for these separately.

Creatures: `{ id, name, count, notes, link, resetsOn }`

Features: `{ id, name, kind, detail, resetsOn }` where `kind` is one of:
`hazard`, `treasure`, `key`, `lever`, `lore`, `other`. `kind` is descriptive only -- the engine never branches
on it.

`resetsOn` is an array drawn from the reset event vocabulary (see below).
Ids must be unique within their own list (`creatures` and `features` are
separate namespaces).

### Rest

`rest: { safety, effect }`, optional. `safety` is one of: `safe`, `unsafe`, `special`.

### Links

`links: [{ kind, label, url }]`. `kind` is one of: `statblock`, `map`, `vtt`, `doc`, `image`, `other`. Every
link needs a `url`.

### Key-gated content

`onKey: { read, detail, gm }`, optional -- shown once the party holds this
tesseract's key. If nothing in a cell is `keyEligible`, this content is
unreachable; the validator does not currently catch that, so check it by eye.

### Engine fields

These are the only fields the generator itself reads. Everything else above
is opaque text handed to the UI.

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `gravity` | `{ type, gravity, desc }` | `type` is one of `Fixed`, `Random`, `Match`, `Special`. `gravity` (0-5) is only read when `type` is `Fixed`; other types compute a value at entry time |
| `role` | one of `start`, `exit`, or `null` | exactly one room in `rooms` must have each role; filler rooms cannot hold a role |
| `keyEligible` | boolean | may hold a cell's key. Defaults `false` for authored rooms, `true` for filler (filler is the usual place to put the ten keys) |
| `includeGroup` | tag | rooms sharing a tag must all be co-located in one tesseract. Max 8 members (a cell holds 8 rooms) |
| `excludeGroup` | tag | rooms sharing a tag may never share a tesseract. Max 5 members (a room occupies 2 of the 10 cells, so at most 5 can stay pairwise disjoint) |
| `maxInstances` | integer ≥ 1 | how many times this content may appear. `null` means "unset": an authored room defaults to a singleton, but naming it in `filler.reusePool` implies unlimited |
| `variants` | `[{ id, ... }]` | distinguishes repeats of the same content from each other; each needs a unique `id` |
| `labelRepeats` | boolean | suffix repeats with `" (II)"`-style labels. Default `true` |

### Room-level actions

Beyond the ones auto-derived from `creatures`/`features`, a room may declare
its own `actions: [{ id, label, resetsOn }]`. `id` must be a slug (so it can't
collide with the namespaced creature/feature actions).

## Filler

`filler` controls how the remaining slots (up to the 40-room total) get filled
once your authored `rooms` are placed.

| field | values | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `strategy` | `templates`, `reuse`, `mixed` | `templates` draws from `filler.templates` (ids in `fillerRooms`); `reuse` repeats entries from `filler.reusePool`; `mixed` does both |
| `templates` | array of `fillerRooms` ids | must exist in `fillerRooms` |
| `reusePool` | array of `rooms` ids, or `"*"` for all | `"*"` is the default |
| `weights` | `{ [id]: number }` | relative draw weight, optional |
| `distribution` | `spread`, `random` | how repeats are spread across the dungeon |

## Pack-level actions

`actions: [{ id, label, resetsOn }]` -- room-independent, always-available
actions (the built-in default is a single `searched` action). `id` must be a
slug.

## Reset events

The built-in vocabulary any `resetsOn` list may reference:
`short-rest`, `long-rest`, `key`, `doors`, `shuffle`.

A pack can add its own via `resetEvents: [{ id, label }]` (top-level, `id`
must be a slug and cannot collide with a built-in event). A custom event
becomes selectable on any `resetsOn` list, but needs a GM-facing trigger
button wired into the app menu to actually fire -- authoring the name here
only makes it choosable.

## Template vars

`{{key}}` tokens inside `read`/`detail`/`gm`/`orientation`/`onKey.*` text,
substituted at display time.

- Always available: `cellColor` (the tesseract the room is
  currently resolved into).
- Reserved, cannot be redeclared by a pack: `variant`
  (spent earlier in generation, before a room reaches display).
- A pack adds its own via top-level `templateVars: [{ key, label }]`. `key`
  must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`.

An unrecognized `{{token}}` in room text is a validator warning, not an
error -- useful if you genuinely need literal braces somewhere.
